_note: Bounds fixed before the notebook is run. Every gate in Session 6 is one of two kinds and there are no others. (1) REPRODUCTION: a digit some frozen artefact already carries -- the corpus manifest, gold_questions.json, reader/MANIFEST.json, toy_index/MANIFEST.json (Deck 6.2's own run), or recorded_rag.json / recorded_agent.json -- which this notebook has to return. A reproduction bound has no preferred direction: it is a comparison against a recorded number, not against a threshold, so it would pass exactly as it does now if reciprocal rank fusion had beaten BM25, if the refusal threshold had cost recall, and if the reader had used its context. (2) PROCEDURE: a property of how the run was done -- hashes checked before a byte is read, the gold anchors proved to name statements the corpus holds, the two reader conditions putting the target at the same window positions, the agent's tool calls passing an allow-list and a gate before they run, the deck's toy matrix hash-checked before a row is read. No gate anywhere in this notebook is on an outcome.
_not_gated: Two results in this lab point the way the lab would rather they did not, and neither is gated in that direction. Block B: fusion does not beat BM25 here (MRR 0.9333 against 0.9583), and gate B4 compares all six recorded MRRs, fusion's included, to the recorded run -- it would pass unchanged if fusion had won. Block C: the reader buys about three per cent from a passage it was just shown, and gate C6 checks the four losses against the recorded run and the procedure that produced them -- it would pass unchanged if the gap had been zero or ten times larger. No gate requires fusion to beat BM25. No gate requires the reader to succeed.
_no_pilot: Nothing in this notebook is graded on a loss, a fit or a seed draw, so there is no seeded pilot file beside this one and no bound below was chosen by watching a distribution. The one torch object in the lab, the 256-character reader, is loaded in eval mode and only ever measured; what is gated about it is structural -- four file hashes, the parameter count, the context width, and the equality of the window positions across conditions.
_toy_note: Gate B1 (added 20 Oct 2026): Deck 6.2's toy must come back from its own matrix -- the passage count and dimension above, the four toy_index files hash-checked, and the five rows and prompt length the slide printed, which the notebook reads from toy_index/MANIFEST.json (written from figures/numbers_toy.tex). Reproduction only: no gate says which passage ought to win. The five rows are compared as a set, because rows 4 and 5 tie exactly (the same paragraph in two statements).
